cards.hint: Think about which surface measurement could serve as a reference.
cards.quote: We could, in theory, use the total surface area as the reference area.
cards.stem: What area choice is described as possible in theory for lift calculations?

cards.hint: Recall how lift changes in direct proportion to area.
cards.quote: Doubling the area doubles the lift.
cards.stem: What happens to lift when the object area is made larger by doubling?

cards.hint: Think about the component direction compared with flight.
cards.quote: Lift is the component of this force perpendicular to the flight direction.
cards.stem: Relative to the path of motion, how is the lift force oriented?

cards.hint: Recall the moving parts on wings that slide and shift.
options: sliding the flaps backwards along metal tracks
folding the wings flat for storage
cards.quote: This is done by sliding the flaps backwards along metal tracks and shifting the slats forward to increase the wing area.
cards.stem: How do designers increase wing size for takeoff and landing at low velocity?
